title: Can a customer buy more demurrage and detention free time while invoices are overdue?
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category decides whether a customer's overdue demurrage and detention balance blocks the purchase of a free-time upgrade on a per-container record. It applies to every upgrade purchase and to the extension fee charged for it.

## Policy clauses

1. Free-time purchases are judged against the customer's whole demurrage and detention portfolio, not against the one record being upgraded.
2. An upgrade may be bought only when the customer's overdue demurrage and detention balance does not exceed the overdue balance threshold of the product being bought.
3. Balances of other product categories, such as booking or documentation charges, never count toward this balance.

## How the overdue balance is measured

The overdue balance is taken on the handling date from the current state of every record of the customer. It is the total of the balance due on each of the customer's records whose status is invoiced and whose invoice is past due.

- An invoice is past due when the handling date is later than the invoice date plus its payment term, and no submitted dispute stands against it.
- The payment term is the payment term of that record's product, counted in calendar days from the invoice date; when the customer is credit-approved and the customer's credit days are longer, the credit days are used instead.
- An invoice under a submitted dispute is not past due.

The measure is read from the line's records (the customer's records, their status and balance, the invoice dates and the customer's credit days) before the purchase is made.

## Decision checklist

| Question | Where it is answered | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Which records count? | The customer's records in invoiced status with an invoice past due and no submitted dispute | Only their balance due is added up |
| Which term applies to each invoice? | The product term, or the customer's longer credit days when credit-approved | Decides whether the invoice is past due |
| Which threshold applies? | The threshold of the product being bought | Compared with the total |
| Result | Total above the threshold | Purchase blocked |
| Result | Total equal to or below the threshold | Not blocked by this policy |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical figures)

- With an illustrative threshold of USD 1000.00 on the product being bought, an overdue total of exactly USD 1000.00 does not exceed it, so this policy does not block the purchase; a total of USD 1000.01 exceeds it and blocks it.
- On the last day of an invoice's payment term the invoice is not yet past due, because the handling date is not later than the end of the term; from the following day it is past due.
- A customer who is not credit-approved is judged on the product term alone, whatever credit days appear on the profile.
- A disputed invoice still awaiting its decision adds nothing to the overdue total, however old it is.
